title: Italy Sound Out Pep Guardiola for National Team Manager Role After World Cup Exit
excerpt: The Italian Football Federation has made initial contact with the former Manchester City and Barcelona manager as it searches for a new direction after the Azzurri's disappointing World Cup campaign.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Italy's football federation has approached Pep Guardiola for the national team manager position.
  • Guardiola left Manchester City after nearly a decade, seeking a new challenge.
  • Italy aims for a fresh direction after a disappointing World Cup exit.
  • Hiring Guardiola would be a significant move for international football management.
  • The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) has made initial contact with Pep Guardiola about becoming Italy's next national team manager
  • Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of the 2025-26 season after nearly a decade, citing the need for a new challenge
  • Italy are searching for a new direction after their World Cup campaign ended in the knockout rounds
  • The appointment would make Guardiola one of the few elite club managers to take a major international job at the peak of his career

Italy Come Calling

The Italian Football Federation has sounded out Pep Guardiola about taking charge of the Azzurri, according to ESPN, in what would be one of the most significant managerial appointments in international football history.

Guardiola, 55, left Manchester City at the end of the 2025-26 season after nearly a decade at the Etihad Stadium, during which he won six Premier League titles, a Champions League, and established City as the dominant force in English football. In a candid interview with Mundo Deportivo, he explained his departure as a need for renewal — both for himself and for the club.

Italy's interest comes as the four-time World Cup winners search for a new manager following a disappointing tournament in the United States and Canada. The Azzurri were eliminated in the knockout rounds, extending a pattern of underperformance that has haunted Italian football since their shock failure to qualify for the 2018 World Cup.

> **"The Azzurri have historically thrived under tactically sophisticated managers who can impose a coherent style on a talented but inconsistent squad."**

"The Azzurri have historically thrived under tactically sophisticated managers who can impose a coherent style on a talented but inconsistent squad."

Why Guardiola

Guardiola's record speaks for itself. Across spells at Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Manchester City, he has won 11 league titles, two Champions League trophies, and fundamentally reshaped how the game is played at the highest level. His positional play philosophy — built on ball retention, spatial manipulation, and relentless pressing — has influenced an entire generation of coaches.

For Italy, the appeal goes beyond trophies. The Azzurri have historically thrived under tactically sophisticated managers who can impose a coherent style on a talented but inconsistent squad. Guardiola's ability to develop young players, build systems around available talent rather than predetermined formations, and instil a winning mentality aligns with what the FIGC is seeking.

"I needed something different. After nine years at City, I needed to feel challenged again, to start something new. That doesn't diminish what we built — it honours it."

— Pep Guardiola, speaking to Mundo Deportivo

The International Question

National team management represents a fundamentally different challenge from club football. Guardiola would have limited time with players, no ability to recruit, and long periods between competitive matches. It is a role that has historically attracted managers at the twilight of their careers rather than those at the peak — which is precisely why the move would be so remarkable.

However, Guardiola has spoken repeatedly about his admiration for Italian football culture. He studied Italian tactical traditions during his sabbatical in New York before joining Bayern Munich, and has cited Arrigo Sacchi and Marcello Lippi among his formative influences.

What It Means for Football

If Guardiola accepts, the appointment would send shockwaves through the football world. Italy, with their deep pool of technical talent emerging from Serie A's renewed competitiveness, would become immediate contenders for Euro 2028 and the 2030 World Cup.

For Indian football fans — a rapidly growing demographic that follows European football passionately — the move would add another compelling storyline to an international calendar that is increasingly central to the sport's global appeal. The Indian Super League has drawn tactical inspiration from Guardiola's methods, and his potential move to the international stage would only amplify that influence.

Guardiola has not publicly commented on Italy's approach. Talks remain at a preliminary stage, and other candidates are reportedly under consideration. But the mere fact that the conversation is happening signals the scale of Italy's ambition — and Guardiola's willingness to embrace the unfamiliar.
